question: Which specific viral infection is the primary cause of almost all cervical cancer cases?

options.A: Human papillomavirus
options.B: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.C: Hepatitis B virus
options.D: Herpes simplex virus

explanation: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) strains is recognized as the necessary causal agent for the development of cervical cancer. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h2)

question: What do we call the state when a person takes in more calories than they burn?

options.A: Metabolic catabolism
options.B: Negative energy balance
options.C: Nutritional equilibrium
options.D: Positive energy balance

explanation: When energy intake beats energy output, you have extra fuel left over. That's a positive energy balance, which adds weight over time.

question: What is the main reason nurses use a portable bladder scanner at the bedside?

options.A: To measure the exact blood flow to the bladder wall
options.B: To estimate the volume of urine left inside the bladder
options.C: To check the chemical composition of the urine
options.D: To look for physical stones inside the kidneys

explanation: A bladder scanner uses harmless sound waves to check how much urine is trapped inside without sticking anything in. Super handy clinical tool!

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical responsibility of the nurse regarding genetic test results?

options.A: Providing accurate and non-judgmental information
options.B: Respecting the autonomy of the patient in decision-making
options.C: Sharing the results openly with extended family members without consent
options.D: Maintaining strict patient confidentiality to prevent discrimination

explanation: Nurses must protect patient privacy and confidentiality; sharing genetic results without explicit consent violates ethical standards. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h6)

question: A patient with an arm cast complains of an intense itch deep inside. What advice should you give?

options.A: Pour a small amount of baby oil down the cast opening to soothe the skin
options.B: Insert a clean knitting needle gently down the side to scratch the itchy spot
options.C: Use a cool hair dryer breeze directed into the cast opening to relieve itching
options.D: Submerge the entire arm in warm soapy water until the itching stops

explanation: A cool breeze from a hair dryer is a safe trick to ease itching. Never stick objects inside the cast—they can break skin or get stuck!

question: What is the main job of the ovaries in the female body?

options.A: Storing urine before it reaches the bladder
options.B: Producing eggs and female hormones
options.C: Filtering waste from the lower abdomen
options.D: Producing red blood cells during pregnancy

explanation: You got this! The ovaries are our female reproductive glands that make ova (eggs) and important hormones like estrogen and progesterone.

question: Why do nurses prefer using a central venous line instead of a small hand vein when running continuous vasopressor drugs?

options.A: It prevents severe tissue damage if the medication leaks into surrounding tissue
options.B: It allows medications to bypass the liver and filter directly into the kidneys
options.C: It eliminates the need for continuous blood pressure monitoring
options.D: It increases the overall absorption rate in peripheral skeletal muscles

explanation: Vasoactive drugs squeeze vessels so hard that if they leak out of a small hand or arm vein into the skin, they can cut off blood flow and cause the tissue to die (necrosis). Central lines handle these strong drugs safely in big veins!

question: What is one major factor that can make a grieving process much harder?

options.A: Having prior experience coping with minor losses
options.B: Clear understanding of the diagnosis well in advance
options.C: Having a strong social support network
options.D: A sudden and unexpected loss

explanation: Exactly right! When a loss happens out of nowhere, you miss that crucial preparation time, which often makes the grief hit much harder.

question: How does the Hib part of the pentavalent vaccine help protect young children?

options.A: By stopping spasms caused by tetanus spores in the umbilical cord
options.B: By stopping the production of abnormal liver enzymes in blood
options.C: By preventing severe respiratory infections and bacterial meningitis
options.D: By blocking the transmission of the yellow fever mosquito vector

explanation: Well done! Hib (Haemophilus influenzae type b) is a nasty bacteria that causes severe pneumonia and meningitis, which this vaccine successfully stops.

question: Which serious condition involves tissue damage and inflammation in the bowels of a premature baby?

options.A: Retinopathy of prematurity
options.B: Transient tachypnea of the newborn
options.C: Necrotizing enterocolitis
options.D: Intraventricular hemorrhage

explanation: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a tough bowel complication in preemies where parts of the intestine can suffer tissue death. You're mastering complex neonatal nursing topics!

question: What is the primary goal in the medical management of acute gastroenteritis?

options.A: Replacing lost fluids and electrolytes
options.B: Stopping the bowel movements immediately
options.C: Placing the patient on a strict zero-food diet
options.D: Giving strong antibiotics to kill all viruses

explanation: Preventing or correcting dehydration is the single most important intervention to save lives in gastroenteritis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h5)

question: If a patient has severe, rapid diarrhea, how might it affect an oral antibiotic they are taking?

options.A: The medication will absorb much faster due to increased gut activity
options.B: The stomach acid will instantly neutralize the active ingredients
options.C: Absorption may be reduced because the drug passes through too quickly
options.D: The drug will experience zero first-pass metabolism in the liver

explanation: Think of it like a train rushing too fast past a station! If things move through the gut too quickly, the drug doesn't have enough time to hang around and get absorbed.

question: What special chemical is added to the blood collection tube for a fasting blood sugar test to keep the blood cells from eating up the sugar?

options.A: Potassium EDTA
options.B: Sodium fluoride
options.C: Heparin sulfate
options.D: Calcium chloride

explanation: Great job! Sodium fluoride acts as a preservative (glycolytic inhibitor) that stops red blood cells from consuming the glucose in the tube before the lab technician can test it.

question: You tally up the oral pills dispensed for the month and notice the total is higher than the actual stock used. What is your best first step?

options.A: Cross-check the daily registers and tally sheets again to find counting errors
options.B: Submit the higher number anyway to show high community demand
options.C: Report the pharmaceutical company for supplying fewer tablets than stated
options.D: Discard the tally sheets and invent new numbers that match the stock balance

explanation: Exactly right! Always review your source documents first to track down where a simple addition or tally mistake happened.

question: Why can high hospital examination tables be tough for patients with mobility challenges?

options.A: They increase the financial cost of routine blood tests
options.B: They prevent patients with mobility limitations from transferring easily
options.C: They take up too much space in standard nursing stations
options.D: They make it difficult for doctors to hear heart sounds clearly

explanation: Think about a wheelchair user trying to climb up! Fixed high furniture can block access and make simple checks really difficult without proper equipment. You're learning fast!

question: Why does caring for neurological patients involve much more than just giving medications?

options.A: Because nurses must also perform surgical procedures
options.B: Because prevention and lifestyle education are vital at every stage
options.C: Because doctors rarely visit neurological patients
options.D: Because medications are completely ineffective for brain disorders

explanation: Medications are only part of the picture. True neurological care means teaching patients, reducing risks, and preventing complications every step of the way.

question: Which observational tool is best used to grade the quality or frequency of a specific behavior?

options.A: Simple checklist
options.B: Consent form
options.C: Rating scale
options.D: Archival record

explanation: Think of a rating scale as a grading tool. It lets you measure the degree or quality of an action, rather than just noting if it happened or not.

question: How does progestin mainly prevent sperm from reaching an egg?

options.A: By destroying sperm in the vagina
options.B: By increasing the temperature of the uterus
options.C: By blocking the fallopian tubes physically
options.D: By thickening the cervical mucus

explanation: You've got this! Progestin changes the thickness of cervical fluid, creating a strong barrier that makes it very hard for sperm to swim upward.

question: In the popular SBAR communication tool used by healthcare workers, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Behavior
options.B: Breath
options.C: Bedside
options.D: Background

explanation: SBAR is a handy way to report patient info! 'B' stands for Background, giving the listener the essential history leading up to the current moment.

question: Why is teaching self-examination important in male reproductive care?

options.A: It is the only reliable way to diagnose a urinary tract infection
options.B: It replaces the need for any future professional medical visits
options.C: It helps patients detect early changes like lumps or swelling
options.D: It prevents the normal age-related decrease in testosterone

explanation: Correct! Self-exams empower patients to notice small changes right away, leading to quicker medical help and better health results.

question: A patient is treated for scabies in your clinic. What must you tell them about the rest of people living in their house?

options.A: Family members should take oral antibiotics to prevent secondary boils
options.B: Household members only need treatment if they sleep in the same bed
options.C: Only family members who are scratching should visit the clinic for cream
options.D: All household contacts must be treated at the same time, regardless of symptoms

explanation: You've got it! Because scabies spreads before itching starts, treating everyone under the roof at the same time is the only way to kick it out for good.

question: What is your immediate action if the patient feels sharp pain while you are flushing their ear?

options.A: Push the syringe faster to clear the blockage
options.B: Lower the temperature of the water
options.C: Stop the irrigation procedure right away
options.D: Ask the patient to lie flat on the bed

explanation: Pain is a warning sign of injury! Stop immediately to protect your patient from further harm. You're doing great learning this.

question: A client gets mild sedation to stay calm during a long MRI. What must the nurse watch most closely?

options.A: Breathing rate and oxygen levels
options.B: Bowel sounds in all four abdominal areas
options.C: The exact room temperature
options.D: How fast the client can walk afterward

explanation: Sedatives can slow down breathing, so keeping an eye on the patient's respiratory rate and oxygen is top priority!

question: How would you simply describe a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: Any gestation that lasts longer than thirty-six weeks
options.B: A pregnancy that automatically ends in a surgical delivery
options.C: Any pregnancy that occurs in a woman older than twenty years
options.D: A pregnancy where the health of the mother or baby is at increased risk

explanation: You've got this! A high-risk pregnancy just means there are extra health factors that need closer watch to keep both mum and baby safe.

question: What does an autoclave mainly use to achieve full sterilization?

options.A: Dry scorching hot air
options.B: Toxic formaldehyde gas
options.C: Ultraviolet light rays
options.D: Moist heat under pressure

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam, which packs enough heat to rapidly destroy all germs and spores.

question: Why does the scope of standing orders differ between a small health post and a large health center?

options.A: Patients in urban areas refuse to be treated using standard nursing protocols
options.B: Larger health centers do not trust their nurses to use simple treatment protocols
options.C: Government regulations forbid rural clinics from using any form of written guidelines
options.D: Smaller posts have fewer equipment, drugs, and advanced staff available on site

explanation: The scope of a standing order must always match the available resources, diagnostic tools, and staff training level of that specific facility. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h3)

question: A mother stops bringing her baby for immunizations because health workers shouted at her for arriving late last month. What type of factor caused this default?

options.A: Severe natural vaccine reactions
options.B: System-related facility barriers
options.C: Genetic predisposition to disease
options.D: Biological immunity resistance

explanation: Poor staff attitudes and hostile clinic environments are system-level barriers that drive caregivers away from health facilities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic, go-to sign of leprosy?

options.A: Enlarged lymph nodes in the neck
options.B: Severe joint pain and morning stiffness
options.C: High fever and generalized body rash
options.D: Definite loss of sensation in a skin patch

explanation: Correct! A pale or reddish skin patch that has completely lost its feeling is a major clue for leprosy.

question: A staff nurse wants to move from a general ward into the busy Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Which benefit of continuing education makes this possible?

options.A: Reducing hospital expenses
options.B: Lowering patient admission rates
options.C: Promoting specialization
options.D: Simplifying medical records

explanation: Specialization gives you the exact skills and confidence you need to step into advanced areas like the ICU or theatre. You can grow your career step by step!

question: Why are pregnant women at a much higher risk of getting severe malaria?

options.A: They spend more time outdoors during peak mosquito biting hours
options.B: They experience natural immunological changes that lower resistance to the parasite
options.C: They are completely allergic to standard antimalarial medications
options.D: Their bodies produce extra iron that feeds the malaria parasite directly

explanation: Correct! Pregnancy naturally shifts the immune system to protect the baby, which unfortunately makes it easier for the malaria parasite to take hold.

question: Which dressing works best for a wound that has heavy bleeding or fluid drainage?

options.A: Dry gauze pad
options.B: Transparent film
options.C: Hydrocolloid wafer
options.D: Alginate dressing

explanation: Alginates come from seaweed and are superstars at soaking up lots of fluid while turning into a soft gel that keeps the wound bed happy.

question: A teenager living with chronic obesity faces a much higher risk of developing which condition early in life?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Type 2 diabetes
options.C: Type 1 diabetes
options.D: Pernicious anemia

explanation: You got it! Extra body fat makes the body struggle with insulin, putting teens with obesity at a higher risk for type 2 diabetes.

question: What is a major risk if a patient goes home without proper family training and home preparation?

options.A: Immediate complete recovery of motor function
options.B: Lower levels of caregiver stress
options.C: Decreased need for community follow-up care
options.D: High rates of preventable rehospitalization

explanation: Without preparation, families may struggle at home, leading to setbacks that unfortunately send the patient right back to the hospital.

question: What is the main biological goal of puberty during adolescence?

options.A: Completion of prefrontal cortex myelination
options.B: Rapid increase in bone mineral density only
options.C: Attaining sexual maturity and reproductive capacity
options.D: Stabilization of adult personality traits

explanation: You got this! Puberty is simply the body's natural transition to reach sexual maturity and the ability to reproduce.

question: What is the main goal of delivering an electrical shock during defibrillation?

options.A: To reset chaotic heart muscle activity and let a normal rhythm restart
options.B: To restart a completely flatlined heart during asystole
options.C: To force the heart valves to open and close manually
options.D: To speed up a dangerously slow resting heart rate

explanation: Think of the shock as a quick reset button! It momentarily stops the heart's chaotic electrical signals all at once, giving the natural pacemaker a chance to step back in and start a normal rhythm.

question: A student nurse uses her password to log into the EMR and opens the chart of a famous musician on another floor just out of curiosity. What has happened here?

options.A: A helpful act of teamwork to see if the patient needs extra visitors
options.B: A routine computer system update performed by the IT department
options.C: An unauthorized privacy breach that can be tracked by audit software
options.D: Standard nursing practice for checking hospital bed occupancy rates

explanation: Patient privacy is sacred! Opening a chart without a direct clinical reason breaks confidentiality rules and will be flagged by the system.

question: How does a public health nurse's daily role differ from a nurse working on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Agency nurses never interact with actual human patients
options.B: Agency nurses focus on community-wide prevention rather than individual bedside treatment
options.C: Hospital nurses write all national healthcare laws
options.D: Agency nurses only dispense emergency medications

explanation: Well done! Ward nurses care for patients one-on-one at the bedside, while public health nurses look at whole communities and prevention strategies.

question: What causes the yellowish skin color seen in neonatal jaundice?

options.A: An excess of white blood cells in the bloodstream
options.B: A temporary infection of the newborn's liver
options.C: Low levels of iron stored in newborn tissues
options.D: The accumulation of bilirubin in the body

explanation: Bilirubin is a yellow pigment produced when red blood cells break down, and it builds up in the skin and eyes when the baby's body cannot clear it fast enough. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h1)

question: Which of the following is a common misconception about dominant genetic disorders that nurses often correct?

options.A: Lifestyle changes can completely erase a faulty gene
options.B: Genetic conditions never show up in families twice
options.C: Every child of an affected parent will automatically inherit the disease
options.D: Genetic disorders only affect elderly individuals

explanation: With autosomal dominant conditions, each pregnancy carries a specific probability, such as fifty percent, rather than an absolute certainty for every single child. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h3)
